requirements.evidence: All contract pieces exist with the specified signatures: CreateQueue (app/Actions/CreateQueue.php:25-27), UpdateQueue with nullable named params (app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:24-31), SetQueueAccess (app/Actions/SetQueueAccess.php:29-31), QueuePermission with single case Call, QueueAccess model with table, array cast and membership()/queue() relations (app/Models/QueueAccess.php:14-46), factory keeping membership and queue in the same entity (database/factories/QueueAccessFactory.php:26-32), migration with cascade FKs, JSON permissions and unique pair plus down() (migration:14-31). Name trimmed + required|max:255, slug defaults to Str::slug(name), explicit slug slugified, unique per entity with ignore on update (app/Actions/Concerns/ValidatesQueueAttributes.php:23-46). Policy covers create/update/manageAccess/call incl. non-array grant denial (app/Policies/QueuePolicy.php:43-63). CallNextTicket authorizes after lock + active check (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:41); Ticket::call does lock -> inactive -> authorize -> LogicException (app/Models/Ticket.php:107-113). Revoke only logged when rows were deleted (SetQueueAccess.php:65-68). Gap: race mapping only recognises SQLite/MySQL error strings (ValidatesQueueAttributes.php:56-57), and the policy relies on User::membershipFor(), which is not in the diff.

conventions.evidence: Domain writes in app/Actions, each authorizing inside the action via Gate::forUser(...)->authorize (CreateQueue.php:27, UpdateQueue.php:31, SetQueueAccess.php:31); single QueuePolicy as the source of truth; #[Fillable] attribute matching sibling models (QueueAccess.php:14); generator-style migration with reversible down(); audit channel used for grants/revokes and registered in docs/ops/logging.md; docs/business-rules.md, docs/database-schema.md and CHANGELOG 'Added' updated; PHPDoc @throws on touched public methods.

security.evidence: Every action authorizes before validation or writes; the previously unauthenticated CallNextTicket now enforces 'call' in all modes (CallNextTicket.php:41) and Ticket::call authorizes before the already-called LogicException (Ticket.php:110-113). Cross-entity membership/queue pairs rejected (SetQueueAccess.php:43-47); policy requires membership in the queue's entity before reading grants, so a foreign grant row is ignored (QueuePolicy.php:45-62, tested). Permission entries validated as strings in the enum; corrupted JSON denies. $fillable set deliberately.

tests.evidence: Pest tests cover every requirement and failure path: CreateQueueTest (default/explicit slug, trim, 255/256 chars, blank, empty slug, per-entity uniqueness, DB race, owner allowed, employee/non-member/other-entity denied with nothing written), UpdateQueueTest (each field, all-null no-op, own slug, conflict, race, deactivation keeps tickets and blocks issuing, denials), SetQueueAccessTest (upsert, dedupe, revoke, no revoke log when nothing deleted, audit context, unknown and non-string entries, cross-entity, self-grant), QueuePolicyTest (roles, grant on other queue, empty/corrupted grants, outsider with grant), CallNextTicket denial in all three modes and Ticket::call ordering. Existing tests switched to managerOf() rather than weakened. Small mismatch: UpdateQueueTest.php:147 is named 'even one with a call grant' but never grants call.

simplicity.evidence: Lean actions sharing one small trait for name/slug rules; policy helpers isManagerOf/isManager avoid duplication (QueuePolicy.php:65-75). However slugConflictOrRethrow (ValidatesQueueAttributes.php:52-66) hand-parses driver error messages instead of catching Laravel's built-in Illuminate\Database\UniqueConstraintViolationException, which is more code and less portable.

readability.evidence: Small focused methods with clear names (validatedQueueAttributes, slugConflictOrRethrow, isManagerOf), comments where non-obvious (lock order, Ticket.php:95; per-queue serialization in SetQueueAccess), test helpers managerOf/memberOf/grantCall in tests/Pest.php keep tests short. No dead code or debug output.

scope.evidence: Everything serves the task: actions, policy, enum, model, factory, migration, both call-path changes, the required docs and a one-line docs/ops/logging.md entry for the new audit events. No UI, no delete action, no unrelated refactors.

issues.explanation: Unique-violation detection matches only SQLite/MySQL message text, so on another driver (e.g. PostgreSQL 'duplicate key value') a slug race surfaces as a raw QueryException, contrary to requirement 2; catching UniqueConstraintViolationException would be simpler and portable.
Every ability depends on User::membershipFor() and on EntityMembership::role being cast to UserRole, neither of which appears in the diff, so correctness rests on unshown code.
Test is named 'denies an employee, even one with a call grant' but never creates the grant, so it does not check what its name claims.
Audit entries are written inside the DB transaction, so a grant or revoke could be logged even if the commit later fails.

review.summary: The change adds CreateQueue, UpdateQueue and SetQueueAccess actions, the queue_access table/model/factory, the QueuePermission enum and QueuePolicy, and enforces the call ability in both CallNextTicket and Ticket::call in the required order, with docs and thorough tests. It closely follows the contract and project conventions; the main weaknesses are a driver-specific string match for unique-index races instead of Laravel's UniqueConstraintViolationException and reliance on an unshown User::membershipFor helper, so it is approvable with small fixes.
